chunks: From him, from Fazalah, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Life and death are two creations from the creations of Allah. So when death comes and enters into the human being, it does not enter into anything except that life has exited from it.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between life and death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) elucidates that life and death are distinct divine creations, illustrating their mutual exclusivity by noting that death's entry into a person coincides with life's simultaneous exit. This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the ontological transition of the soul, a concept central to Shia theological discussions on the nature of existence and the moment of passing. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the physical and spiritual mechanics of mortality in Islamic anthropology.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Fazalat, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The life and the death are two creatures from the creatures of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, So when the death comes and enters into the human being, it does not enter into anything except that the live exits from it’.
en.sarwar: 34. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Fadalah from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Life and death are two creatures of the creatures of Allah. When death comes then it enters in man. In whatever things death enters, life goes out of that place.’”
